texts.value: Catalyzes both the synthesis of cyclic ADP-beta-D-ribose (cADPR) from NAD(+), and its hydrolysis to ADP-D-ribose (ADPR) (PubMed:7805847). Cyclic ADPR is known to serve as an endogenous second messenger that elicits calcium release from intracellular stores, and thus regulates the mobilization of intracellular calcium (Probable). May be involved in pre-B-cell growth (Probable)
ADP-ribosyl cyclase and cADPR hydrolase activities are both activated by Zn(2+) or Mn(2+), and inhibited by Cu(2+), while Mg(2+) and Ca(2+) do not have any significant influence
Expressed in various tissues including placenta, lung, liver and kidney
Belongs to the ADP-ribosyl cyclase family
